entries.proposition: The abstract and Discussion list the ADRD-PD shared loci by a name that includes WWOX while the nearest gene to the WWOX-locus variant in Table 2 is MAF.
entries.snippet: five with ADRD and PD (near LCORL, CLU, SETD1A/KAT8, WWOX, and GRN)

entries.proposition: The WWOX-locus lead variant is an ADRD lead variant that is only Bonferroni-level for PD, in the same direction with the same small odds ratio.
entries.snippet: rs450674 had the same direction and magnitude of association with both disorders (ADRD OR = 1.04, p = 3.2 × 10−8; PD OR = 1.04, p = 2.1 × 10−4), and colocalization supported a shared causal variant (80.5% chance).
entries.anchor: Results, Genetic risk loci shared between ADRD and PD, para 4

entries.proposition: The authors attach WWOX to the variant only because it is the only other coding gene within 500 kb of a variant lying downstream of MAF.
entries.snippet: Besides MAF, the only other coding gene within 500 kilobases is the oxidoreductase WWOX, involved in the regulation of apoptosis.

entries.proposition: The WWOX literature offered for AD is knockdown-in-vitro and knockout-mouse, and the authors concede the knockout is not a realistic model of a common-variant effect.
entries.snippet: though Wwox knockout may not be a realistic model for the much gentler perturbation of WWOX expression likely to be effected by a common GWAS variant

entries.proposition: The only dopaminergic datum offered for WWOX is the MPP+ toxin study, cited as WWOX phosphorylation contributing to neuronal apoptosis; no dopaminergic neuron, dopamine or catecholamine measurement is made in the paper.
entries.snippet: Supporting its relevance to PD, WWOX phosphorylation contributed to neuronal apoptosis upon treatment with the dopaminergic neurotoxin 1-methyl-4-phenyl-pyridinium (MPP +), a model of PD [57].

entries.proposition: Causal-gene assignment is explicitly not established by the study.
entries.snippet: Our hypotheses about causal gene candidates should not be treated as definitive.

entries.proposition: Sharing a causal variant is not sharing a causal gene.
entries.snippet: We note that sharing a causal variant is not at all the same as sharing a causal gene

entries.proposition: The paper's own stated limits: coloc assumes at most one causal variant per locus; ADRD includes proxy cases.
entries.snippet: Second, our colocalization analysis assumes that each disorder has at most one causal variant per locus.

entries.proposition: The WWOX-locus colocalization probability is stated as 80.5% in Table 2 and 80.4% in the Discussion.
entries.snippet: CLU (88.4% chance), WWOX (80.4% chance), and LCORL (65.3% chance)
